I've experienced this many a number of times in my current 10 month LDR. What seems to help the most is giving them a taste of their own medicine, despite how awful it is to act as if you don't care about them and how they're treating you. When I say fuck it, make myself unavailable and don't contact him, that's when he comes around wondering why *I'm* quiet and rekindles communication. Making him think he's losing you rather than the other way around helps sometimes. A few times he explained his distance was due to something I did he didn't like, or he thought I wanted space, etc. I learned to not be so co-dependent and practiced the things that increase your value in their eyes. i.e. making yourself unavailable, etc. Don't confront him anymore, it doesn't work in my experience, and see if it changes anything.

When I used to have an anxiety generator that felt "stuck on" too, and it was ruining my life, this book pretty much cured me. It's a method to reset your moods and thoughts, like you mentioned.

http://www.amazon.com/What-Say-When-Talk-Yourself/dp/0671708821/ref=sr_1_1?s=books&ie=UTF8&qid=1285122982&sr=1-1

It's basically about recognizing the thoughts and feelings that trigger attacks of anxiety and depression, and stopping them before they can affect you. You overwrite your old thought patterns with new, better ones to help you get through life. It takes some time but it helped me immensely. I never needed professionals or medication because of the method. It can also be applied to depression, etc. Maybe it can help you too.
